To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LF is a multifunctional molecule that can play a role in cancer progression and that LF can represent a useful marker for the diagnosis of some human tumors.
LF immunoreactivity has been found in a large number of human tumors and that it may have a role as a tumor marker in some neoplasms.

LF is expressed in different human neoplastic districts and that it has a role in the modulation of tumor growth, in the modulation of the tumor microenvironment and in the regulation of tumor angiogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
LF distribution, localization and function in different human tissues and tumors.
the LF immunohistopathological distribution in human neoplasias and the LF function in the neoplastic process.
the LF immunohistopathological pattern in different human tumors and with the role of LF in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LF expression is related to the presence of an inflammatory reaction in the neoplasm, which is often the case, or to the presence of a specific cell lineage, which is the other case.
LF, in addition to its iron-binding activity, may play an active role in cancer, both in tumor cells as well as in tumor stroma.
LF has a dual function, as an iron transporter and as a multifunctional protein, which may act in the control of cell growth and differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LF has an important role in cancer development, progression and metastases, and its presence could be a useful marker in the diagnosis and treatment of human neoplastic diseases.
, in general, LF has been demonstrated in all neoplastic tissues investigated, with a different immunohistochemical distribution, according to the tumor histotype and to the site.
LF is a multifunctional protein with a wide range of biological activities, and its role in the pathogenesis and/or progression of human neoplastic diseases is still to be clarified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LF immunoreactivity is present in most of the human tumors, and its expression can be considered as a general feature of cancer.
LF has a dual function in cancer: on one hand, it can be considered a tumor marker, and on the other, it is involved in tumor progression and aggressiveness.
